editorial:
Flight (2012) follows Whip Whitaker, a skilled pilot who hides a serious drinking and drug problem behind confident flying. When his plane suffers a mechanical failure, he pulls off an unbelievable crash landing that saves most passengers. The story then shifts from disaster to personal fallout, as investigators dig into his life and he struggles to face the truth. It feels tense, emotional, and grounded, with a strong focus on character rather than just spectacle.

Denzel Washington gives a powerful performance that carries the film, and the crash sequence is gripping without feeling overdone. The pacing is steady, though some scenes feel heavy and uncomfortable. If you enjoy serious dramas about flawed people, this is a great pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Whip stops hiding and tells the truth at the hearing, admitting he was drunk and high during the crash. He accepts prison time instead of letting others take the blame. The twist is that his honesty finally breaks his denial, and he begins rebuilding his life while serving his sentence. It ends with him speaking to fellow inmates about his mistakes.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves serious dramas about flawed people and strong acting.
